rows: Updating an existing file requires the current blob SHA, and conflicting create/update/delete operations must be serialized.
A per-file SHA does not enforce forward-only application state or one atomic multi-file transition.
A multi-file commit is constructed from blobs, a tree, a commit with the current parent, and a ref update.
The caller must still compare the expected parent/ref and verify readback.
Git references identify branch tips and can be read and updated through the REST API.
Application-level generation and monotonic-state rules are not automatic.
A commit binds a tree to parent commit identities and metadata.
A commit timestamp alone does not prove ordered application-state transitions.
A tree can bind multiple file paths to exact blob objects before one commit is created.
Tree creation must use the intended base tree or omitted files can be lost.
Blob objects identify exact file content stored in Git.
Blob identity does not validate JSON schema or cross-file semantic consistency.
GitHub REST requests can pin an API version for stable behavior.
API versioning does not replace repository-state optimistic concurrency.
Conditional requests and serial mutation reduce conflicts and unnecessary work.
HTTP caching validators are not a substitute for a domain generation identifier.
Atomic push can update all refs or none, and explicit force-with-lease checks an expected old ref value.
A normal fast-forward push does not validate application-level increment monotonicity.
update-ref supports expected-old-object checks and reference transactions.
Worktree file comparison alone is not an authoritative remote CAS.
rev-parse resolves exact revisions and repository paths.
Resolved revisions must be recorded in every generation that claims remote authority.
hash-object computes Git object identity from exact bytes.
Hash identity does not prove path authorization or state freshness.
Porcelain output is designed for stable scripting of index and worktree state.
A clean worktree does not prove that distributed control files form one generation.
Git diff can compare tree, index and worktree states.
Cross-document JSON invariants require separate validation.
git fsck verifies object connectivity and validity within the object database.
Repository integrity does not establish business workflow completion.
File.Replace replaces a destination file with another file and can retain a backup.
Single-file replacement does not create a multi-file transaction.
Flush(true) requests buffered data be flushed through intermediate file buffers.
Directory entry durability and remote Git publication remain separate.
Windows can retrieve the final normalized path for an opened file handle.
The file must be opened under an explicit reparse-point and access policy.
File.Move changes a file or directory location and may have filesystem-specific behavior.
A move operation does not itself prove crash-consistent generation switching.
PowerShell converts JSON objects into PSCustomObject values and duplicate names can collapse.
Strict control records need duplicate-key, type and schema rejection before use.
JSON object names should be unique and interoperable numbers exclude NaN and Infinity.
The RFC does not define this project’s cross-file state machine.
HTTP defines representation metadata and conditional request semantics including validators.
ETag and Last-Modified do not replace Git commit and application generation binding.
RFC 3339 defines an interoperable Internet timestamp profile with explicit offsets.
Timestamp syntax alone does not prove monotonicity, freshness or trusted clock source.
JSON Schema defines structural validation vocabulary and resource identifiers.
Schema validation must be combined with exact hashes, generation and transition invariants.
